evidence.positive: With the shipped build (1087f571b) and the datasource-proxy query logger set to DEBUG via POST /actuator/loggers plus Postgres log_statement=all, posted the rormc-ras-acetaminophen.hl7 fixture (PMRN rewritten to 99000001, RXA-3 set to now) to POST /api/admin/hl7-inbound-messages/send with X-Tenant-Id mayo-mayo. App log showed 'Administration matched no operation window', then 'Persisted HL7-sourced MedicationAdministration id=01a17977-1556-7d4f-8199-a6d4f6de243b (wasUpdate=false)', then the after-commit hook ran (EventService 'Handling event MedicationAdministrationEvent', ScheduledRuleEngine 'No operation for this administration'). DB row: tracking_id NULL, operation_id NULL. In that window the app logged 114 SQL statements and Postgres 190 executes, and exactly zero of them touched rule_fired_results, in both logs. Repeated after the red-check restore with PMRN 99000003 (new order id): persisted id=01a1797a-559b-7ec1-a02a-e1d083f2ffa0, 110 SQL statements logged, zero against rule_fired_results.
evidence.negative: Resent the same order/sequence for PMRN 99000001 (new MSH-10), which takes the edit path that mints a tracking id on an administration that had none. App log: 'Persisted ... id=01a17977-1556-7d4f-8199-a6d4f6de243b (wasUpdate=true)', DB row now tracking_id=01a17977-c409-7e02-8dff-7c8830a16fda. The compliance lookup DID run and had the shipped shape in both logs: 'from rule_fired_results rfr1_0 join rule_execution_contexts rec1_0 on rec1_0.id=rfr1_0.rule_execution_context_id where rec1_0.tracking_id=?' with Params:[(01a17977-c409-7e02-8dff-7c8830a16fda)]; Postgres DETAIL: parameters: $1 = '01a17977-c409-7e02-8dff-7c8830a16fda'. So an administration that carries a tracking id still gets its lookup, as an inner join driven by the bound id, and no 'left join' or 'is null' appeared.
evidence.red_check: Ran the pre-fix code. Took the parent-commit versions of RuleComplianceService (no null guard; @Slf4j written out as an explicit LoggerFactory logger) and AbstractRuleResult (@ManyToOne without optional=false; lombok getters/setters written out), compiled them in the container with its JDK 25 javac against /app/classes:/app/libs/*, backed up the shipped RuleComplianceService.class (md5 449018d390c5b11f72049eb8b757476c) to /tmp/prefix/backup, copied both pre-fix classes into /app/classes (the models class shadows the orci-models jar because /app/classes precedes /app/libs on the Jib classpath), restarted the container at 18:28:59Z, re-enabled the query logger, and sent a fresh untracked administration (PMRN 99000002, new order id). It persisted (id=01a17979-50b2-7ec3-aa84-faf7c4d4e7bd, tracking_id NULL) and the after-commit hook issued, in both the app log and the Postgres log: 'select ... from rule_fired_results rfr1_0 left join rule_execution_contexts rec1_0 on rec1_0.id=rfr1_0.rule_execution_context_id where rec1_0.tracking_id is null' with Params:[()] - the exact LEFT JOIN + IS NULL scan the ticket describes. Reverted: moved the AbstractRuleResult override out of /app/classes, copied the shipped RuleComplianceService.class back (md5 re-verified 449018d390c5b11f72049eb8b757476c, models directory back to only 'weight'), restarted at 18:30:04Z, re-ran the positive case (PMRN 99000003) with zero rule_fired_results queries. Grepping the whole container log for the signature finds it only at 18:29:16Z, inside the red window.

red_check_signature: left join rule_execution_contexts rec1_0 on rec1_0.id=rfr1_0.rule_execution_context_id where rec1_0.tracking_id is null
caveats: The tracked (negative) case used the HL7 edit-resend path to mint a tracking id on an administration with no operation, so the lookup ran with the id bound but matched no firings; the in-operation-window path where rules actually fire and ComplianceResults get written was not exercised here (its behaviour is unchanged by this fix).
Only the SQL shape was verified (inner join + bound id vs left join + IS NULL); the index-usage and Aurora ACU-load claims cannot be observed on this instance, whose rule tables are empty.
The pre-fix AbstractRuleResult was compiled with lombok accessors written out by hand, so the swapped class is behaviourally but not byte-for-byte the parent commit's.
SQL observation depended on turning on the datasource-proxy query logger at runtime through /actuator/loggers and Postgres log_statement=all; both were left enabled on the disposable instance.

automation.assessment: The merged PR already locks in both halves at unit level: RuleComplianceServiceGuardTest verifies a null tracking id never touches the repository (mocked), and RuleFiredResultRepositoryTest captures the generated SQL with a StatementInspector and asserts an inner join on rule_execution_contexts. What is not covered is the end-to-end path the ticket is actually about: an HL7 administration persisted outside an operation window reaching the after-commit hook and issuing no rule_fired_results query at all. DefaultHL7ProcessingContextSaveMedAdminIntegrationTest already drives saveMedAdmin against a real database, so that assertion is cheap to add there with the same StatementInspector pattern.
proposed_tests: DefaultHL7ProcessingContextSaveMedAdminIntegrationTest: saveMedAdmin with operation=null commits, then assert via a StatementInspector that no statement referencing rule_fired_results ran and that the administration's tracking_id is null (goes red when the null guard in RuleComplianceService is removed).

Same test class: resend the same order/sequence (edit path) and assert the single rule_fired_results statement contains ' join rule_execution_contexts ' with the minted tracking id bound and no 'left join' or 'is null' (guards both the inner-join mapping and that tracked administrations still get their lookup).

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: An HL7 administration outside any operation window persisted with a null tracking id and the after-commit hook issued no query against rule_fired_results, in both the application SQL log and the Postgres statement log.
Negative: An administration carrying a tracking id still ran the compliance lookup, as an inner join on rule_execution_contexts with the id bound.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix RuleComplianceService and AbstractRuleResult classes into the running container made the same untracked administration issue the LEFT JOIN ... tracking_id IS NULL scan, and restoring the shipped classes made it disappear again.

Automation: The PR's unit and repository tests cover both halves; an end-to-end assertion on the HL7 save path that no rule_fired_results statement runs for an untracked administration is proposed.
